 MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 01.12.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.396/2020 ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MACT, BENGALURU SCCH-11, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 01.12.2021 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH- 11) in MVC No.396/2020.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 13.12.2019 at about 12.45pm,
when the claimant was riding a two wheeler bearing Registration No.KA- 11 L-5467, near Rudrakshipura Village, Maddur Taluk, at that time the driver of I20 Asta bearing Registration No.TS-07 GC- NC: 2023:KHC:45235 5626 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant lost balance and fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.

Sri.Krishnappa H.T vs Sri.Amitabha Saha on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191238925/
2 3.
The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges, etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. On service of notice, both the respondents have appeared through their counsel and filed written statements.
Respondent No.1 - Owner of the offending vehicle, in his written statement denied the averments made in the claim petition.
He disputed the manner of accident, age of injured and quantum of compensation claimed under different heads.

He admits that the Car belongs to him,
which was insured with respondent No.2 and the insurance policy was in force at the time of accident and the driver of the Car was having a valid license to drive the vehicle.
He pleaded that the petition itself is NC: 2023:KHC:45235 false and frivolous in the eye of law.
It was further pleaded that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the two wheeler by the claimant himself.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Respondent No.2 - Insurance company of the offending vehicle, in their written statement denied the averments made in the claim petition.
They contend that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective license at the time of accident and respondent No.1 and thereby contravened the provisions of the MV Act.

It was further pleaded that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the two wheeler by the claimant himself and he is not having valid and effective driving license to ride the Motor Cycle.
They admitted the issuance of policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 to the offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
They prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant himself was examined as PW1 and Dr. Nagaraj.B.N., was examined as PW2 and got exhibited NC: 2023:KHC:45235 documents, namely, Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
On behalf of the respondents, respondent No.1 was examined himself as RW1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance company did not adduce any evidence on its behalf.
7. The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.5,87,315/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and held both the respondents jointly and severally liable to pay compensation and directed the respondent No.2 - Insurance company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved

,
present appeal has been filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

8. Sri Tejas N., learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, due to the accident the claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
He examined the doctor as PW-2.

The doctor in his evidence has stated that NC:
2023:KHC:45235 the claimant has suffered physical disability of lower limb at 45%

Sri . Krishnappa H.T vs Sri.Amitabha Saha on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191238925/
3 and whole body physical disability with respect to the right lower limb at 15% and whole body disability at 23%.

The Tribunal assessed whole body disability at 12%,
which is on the lower side.
b) Secondly, due to the accident the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and he was inpatient for a period of 9 days and he has suffered lot of pain during treatment,
he has to suffer the disability and unhappiness through out his life.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal for pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses, is on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation by allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, Sri Pradeep B. the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised following counter contentions:
a) Firstly, even though the doctor has assessed whole body disability at 23% he assessed the NC: 2023:KHC:45235 disability to lower limb at 45%.
Considering the evidence of doctor and medical records, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the whole body disability at 12%.

b) Secondly, considering the evidence of the doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses are just and reasonable.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

c) in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

sentences.text: Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

11. It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 13.12.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle - I20 Asta bearing Registration No.TN-07 GC-5626 by its driver.
(d) Fracture of right proximal fibula.
12. The claimant has examined the doctor as PW2.

In his evidence he has deposed that the claimant has suffered physical disability to the lower limb at 45% and to that whole body physical disability with respect to right lower limb is at 15% and whole body disability at 23%.
Considering the evidence of doctor and medical records, age and avocation of the claimant, I am of the opinion that whole body disability has to be assessed at 15%.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed monthly income of the claimant at Rs.14,000/- per month.
The NC: 2023:KHC:45235 multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 years is '13'.
Accordingly, loss of future earning has been re-
assessed as follows:
Due to the accident the claimant has suffered the aforesaid injuries and he was inpatient for a period of 9 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during the treatment and he has to suffer with the disability and unhappiness through out his life.

Considering the evidence of the doctor and the injury suffered by the claimant, I am inclined to enhance the compensation for loss of amenities from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
14.
Loss of income during the laid up period has to be granted for a period of three months.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.42,000/- (Rs.14,000/- X 3 months)
under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
15.
The claimant was treated as inpatient for 9 days in the hospital and thereafter, has received further treatment.
Hence, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded under the head of 'food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges' from Rs3,600/- to Rs.10,000/-.
Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

17. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

 up period

 amenities  Loss of future income 2,62,080/- 3,27,600/-

18.

In the result, the following order is passed:
- 11 -  NC: 2023:KHC:45235  ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of  Rs.6,93,235/-.
d) In view of judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE' (supra), the enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.

e) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization,
